notes.title: v2.0 Has Arrived!
notes.content:
aeiou here, let me be the first to welcome you to Cardaire 2.0! Be sure to talk to the collector, as he may have some stuff for you if you've already got an active save file.

There's SO MUCH to go over with this update, but here's the highlights:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121936/1ba57cd70de3e37dfb84abfc081bce68f72676cd.png[/img]

Stick around after the patch notes for a little thank you and thoughts on where we go from here.

[h2]Patch Notes[/h2]

[h3]AI Updates:[/h3]
There is quite a lot to explain in terms of how the enemy AI thinks, so I will get into as much detail as I can here - but there are a BUNCH of systems that were updated to generally function better and make the enemy AI a more worthy opponent.

I want to note the enemy AI is still able to make "mistakes". I find it good for new players to be given edges to learn from these mistakes, and it also is valuable for experienced players as they get to "outsmart" the enemy duelist. This also scales with duelists as the game progresses, with later game duelists and bosses playing better as you go. (The first area AI is not far from it's old state for example, and the final boss plays ALMOST as tight as possible.)

A few of the AI changes include:
- Weighting on where the enemy will play soul cards (For example prioritizing the guard slot to protect themselves, or a terrain slot that would benefit them)
- Prioritizing attacking enemy soul cards when they are at risk of lethal damage

[h3]Content Updates![/h3]
- Added some post game focused areas. (You'll need to beat the main game before accessing most of it. Take the southwest path in Slowflow Road to get there.)
- Added systems to unlock custom card backs for your deck. Go explore and find one you like! (Equip them through your item inventory)
-- Some are found by beating bosses, load junction hub if you already did so and are missing one and it should be placed in your inventory.
- Certain Duelists will now use custom card backs (stylish!)
- Added 3 new promo cards to find. (promo cards don't count for collection level, but are still pretty neat)
- Added a new Fishing Minigame with a few different rewards
- Added the Lucky Draw machine
- Added a  ̶s̶e̶c̶r̶e̶t̶ ̶b̶o̶s̶s̶

[h3]Fixes:[/h3]
- The board will now correctly display when a card's Attack is less than 0
- Fixed an issue that was causing lethal damage to not end the game until the turn was passed
- Fixed a bug with Sally's second duel that would cause the game to softlock if a soul got 0 health from being played on a slot that reduced health
- Fixed a bug with Sally's second duel that would cause soul cards not to take damage
- Updated the artist credit on Graveborne Reaper (Thanks Pan Gaming!)
- Fixed the clipping on some card corners that was causing them to appear square instead of rounded
- Fixed the slot effect for the Quiet Duelist in Frontier Wilds North
- Updated the round 2 and 3 Mini Tourny exit portal colors to better match the floor
- Added in duel comments to some duelists who were missing them
- Added a card to the Final Frontier npc decks so they have a proper 30 cards instead of 29
- Updated Beast Herald's description to note that the card is moved to hand if your board is full
- Corrected a typo in Big Duelist's dialog
- Fixed the Tourny Point Machine only subtracting 1 point when you purchased a 2 point item (whoops)

[h3]Other Changes:[/h3]
- Implemented a pre-loader for images. This should help things run generally faster (Thanks Synrec!)
- Gave Clerk of Soulbinder a unique animation when played
- Mini Tourny opponents now have unique decks that get a bit better as you progress in the tourny
- Made some minor changes to Raine's deck to make it a bit better
- Updated the roll for opening a God Card in a pack
-- Before: 1/150 without lucky dice, 1/100 with
-- Now: 1/100 without lucky dice, 1/50 with

[h2]And a Special Thanks to Viewers Like You...[/h2]

With this update it's my plan to finally put Cardaire down for a while. (With the exception of fixing any bugs it might have brought about)

It's been a dream come true seeing people play and experience Cardaire for the first time. My deepest, biggest, and most sincere thank you to all the players that have shared kind words in a playthough or review. It's meant the world to me.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121936/bcec3a9ea06d189037d4d081a26f10f45e6ce03a.png[/img]

Making Cardaire has been actively on my brain for something like 4 years now. And even now there are endless things I would like to add to it or improve about it, rough edges that make it less appealing to some. But I believe the bumps in a game are what give it character, and don't all need to be sanded down.

And truth be told, the number one thing Cardaire would need for me to continue expanding on it past this update would be a change in game engine and re-making from scratch. (RPGMaker is an amazing engine, but my limited coding skills are only so good at fitting square pegs into round holes.)

I don't know exactly what the future holds for me, and that's kind of exciting. I may or may not come back to Cardaire some day, but that's a decision for future aeiou to make. For the time being I am going to let my creativity wander until I come upon the next project I want to put a larger amount of my time into. I've already got a few ideas that are looking like good seeds to grow a new project from.

So this crazy game called Cardaire is yours now. I hope you find something in it that inspires you in the next thing that you make. 

See you next time Cardaire Duelists

notes.title: Coming Soon: AI Improvements, Cosmetic Options, Post Game Content
notes.content:
[h2]Turn Pass[/h2]

Hello seasoned duelists and fledgling card slingers alike, it's aeiou here. Hope you've had a nice December. Me? Well I've been doing my favorite thing - working on game content :)

It was a really cathartic experience returning to making content for Cardaire post launch. Things moved a bit faster now, and I was able to move with better purpose having seen a wider audience play and react to the game. You never really know what players will have strong positive OR negative reactions to until the game is in their hands.

I'm happy to announce I'll be releasing what I've dubbed the [b]"2.0 Update"[/b] quite soon. With this update I have two major goals:
[olist]
[*] Address the most popular piece of feedback I've gotten about the game (looking at you enemy AI)
[*] Add just a lil' bit more post game content
[/olist]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121936/fc06da69a7be7e450e13df18668c2af9140c015b.png[/img]
(Art by [url=https://x.com/RamaWidjanarko2]Rama Widjanarko[/url])

[h2]What to Expect[/h2]

As much as I would love to make sweeping changes to the in-duel UI or deck editor, the hard truth is that those changes would require a game engine change and remaking the game from scratch. But with that in mind I wanted to do what I can to get the game in the current engine to be as good of an experience as possible.

The #1 thing I've seen mentioned as a requested change is improvement to the enemy AI, so that is the major issue I've taken on with this update.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121936/fef38f2bde66cdd15609e54c5b366874a70f754d.png[/img]

So if [b]you promise[/b] to keep your expectations for the update realistic, here are some things that [b]I can promise[/b] will be in the update:

(did you promise? thank you, we make a good team you and I)

[list]
[*] Improvements to the enemy Duel AI that generally scale as you progress through the game
[*] Some unlockable cosmetics
[*] A new area that offers a bit of post game content for the thirstier grinders
[*] A handful of new Steam Achievements
[*] A few new music tracks
[*] A new (fishing!) minigame
[/list]

[h2]When to Expect It[/h2]

So when can you expect to get your hands on this fine update? Next year? Next Month?

*does a half hearted drum roll on my leg*

[b]January 17th![/b]

That's right, I'm planning on launching this thing in just about 2 weeks. If something really funky happens with playtesting I'll adjust accordingly, but that's the plan for now!

Here's just a tiny little preview image in the mean time.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121936/13b2e625f52b6c7b2f891b6bf2572446e8483fff.png[/img]

[h2]In Other News...[/h2]

That's all I have for the time being Duelists. I'm going to skitter back to my dev cave and get back to work. Here's some other cool Cardaire stuff from the past couple weeks to hold you over.

- aeiou out!

[h3]I Need MORE Single Player Collectable Card Games![/h3]

Pan Gaming over on "the youtubes" posted an excellent video breaking down the magic of single player CCGs, with a focus on Cardaire (that's us!). I can't recommend the video enough, go check it out!

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I0DFS3r-NuE

[h3]Boss Collage[/h3]

One of our own card artists [url=https://bsky.app/profile/spacejamtwo.bsky.social]spacejamtwo (Victoria)[/url] sent me some outstanding art for the holidays that I can't help but share with how sweet it is. Check out those [strike]duelist pin machines[/strike] area bosses!

[url=https://bsky.app/profile/spacejamtwo.bsky.social][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121936/d29ebb104dca07af9e8441361286153ec54b91d4.png[/img][/url]

notes.title: Devlog 2: One Piece at a Time
notes.content:
[i]I got it one piece at a time
And it didn't cost me a dime
You'll know it's me when I come through your town
I'm gonna ride around in style
I'm gonna drive everybody wild
'Cause I'll have the only one there is around[/i]

- "One Piece at a Time" Wayne Kemp and Johnny Cash

[h2]One Piece at a Time[/h2]
If ya didn't know I'm aeiou, and I made this thing. From 2020-2023 I went back and forth working on a project I called "Project Electronic Cardboard". It was stuck in a frustrating loop of starting back up and then one thing or anther leading to it being back-burnered again. So I set out into 2024 the goal of finishing it as best I could with the mantra from that ol' country classic "One Piece at a Time". Every day I did a little bit of work, slowly piecing together something that might not be perfect - but was uniquely mine.

This devlog shows just a small amount of that process. I believe making a game is best as a highly iterative process. This means ideas are rapidly prototyped, recycled, or shelved. And the game emerges from that iteration. But each piece along the way is important, as it gets you one step closer to the end product.

[h2]Friendly Mulligan?[/h2]

Where better to start, than our intrepid protagonist Mulligan! Mulligan's design and the first pass at her in game sprite were created by the magnificent [url=https://linktr.ee/geneljumalon]Genel Jumalon[/url]. Genel put on an absolute masterclass in character design with his work creating Mulligan. He began by creating an array of concepts to then be narrowed down based on what best fit the character. I'm still in awe at how he was able to create a lineup of unique silhouettes that all express strong character with minimal detail.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121936/3c97977e8d082ae4f92d81cb52f857d19be859bc.png[/img]

From there the task of choosing a color for her outfit became the next task. In retrospect the other colors look weird on mulligan, but when you are in the throws of character design something as prevalent at the main characters color scheme can drive you crazy. There was a point in time when the orange jacket was the winner, but alas naruto-mulligan was short lived.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121936/52dcec4b20e8b6b0ab88b53c3def41fed2def0f1.png[/img]

I probably asked Genel to render three dozen different color jackets, but eventually the cool blue with purple accents hit the spot. I figured that color would work best against green grass, tan sand, and grey stone - and fit with the greenish blue coloring that was becoming a part of the general card color scheme. With that, the Mulligan we know and love was born.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121936/94f7b44b2d5fc7c1caa44008dc587eba4572c219.png[/img]

[h2]Pixels (No, not the one with Adam Sandler)[/h2]

Working with such a strong design made it all the easier to translate into a pixel art game. Strong features such as Mulligan's hair, slightly oversized jacket, and boots all work as markers for visual design when you are working at a low fidelity visual form like pixel art.

Here we can see the evolution of Mulligan's in game front facing sprite. (With Genel creating (1), and me creating the rest.).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121936/afcb6b9c5efc203781c7ace98113576cb69554c0.png[/img]

As you can see there was quite the shift in the levels of "chibi"ness the sprite went through. Design (2) was created as I first got reinvested in the project in 2024, with the idea for pixel characters with the amount of detail of roughly Gen V of pokemon in a 1x1 format. As I started to play around with it in game though I realized it felt a bit too condensed, so aimed for something closer to the taller 1x2 format of many GBA games. Our Mulligan had a late growth spurt, let's say.

But static sprites are one thing, what really sells a protagonist is a satisfying movement sprite. The thing I spent the most time on was UNDOUBTEDLY the movement of Mulligans Ahoge (her big center hair strand). After a day of getting nowhere with the animation I finally sketched it out on paper while following the wiggle of my hand:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121936/8b2063d8e46591a867c8b68a1928b95d1eee05c2.gif[/img]

This lead me to realizing you really wanted the bottom of the object to move first, and then the rest to follow from the bottom up. This gives the object a sense of weight as it looks like it's pulling on the structure as it sways.

[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121936/62533eced7c0562a3e06167f6f3a824e5b60cd4a.gif][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121936/62533eced7c0562a3e06167f6f3a824e5b60cd4a.gif[/img][/url]

Add a little perspective shift as the arms swing, time the movement to when she dips down to switch feet, and baby you a got a stew going.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121936/b1367b0feaa4a9162f6c0e9bd9cc965f2c42a871.gif[/img]

[h2]It's in the Cards[/h2]

But what's a card game without cards? Well it's just a game, and that's mighty boring if you ask me. Through the design process the card frame shifted too many times to count with tiny adjustments and tweaks to make the card convey the information it needed to. Here are some of the big things I learned to be important as the design evolved:

[list]
[*] Don't work against existing conventions. You can fight your style battles elsewhere. Do what's expected and show cost in the top left in an orb, and Atk/HP marked with the expected symbols.
[*] The art is the most important thing players use to recognize cards (Even more so than the name!). It deserves to take up a large portion of the frame.
[*] Outline colors on text are great for legibility, but can make a design look tacky when overused.
[/list]

The card frame through development:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121936/45fb559d125dd89145c7c214c9ecb2166bb4ed5c.png[/img]

You may notice the final card design shrink's it's height a bit. This is to match the exact aspect ratio of a standard trading card, as it would make buying things like sleeves for physical cards much easier (not that physical cards are a current plan, but future proofing doesn't hurt :D )

[h2]Work of Art[/h2]
Aaaaaaaaand what's a card without art? I was fortunate to work with several amazing artists who made their impact on the overall card art style for the game, but want to highlight [url=https://x.com/RamaWidjanarko2]Rama Widjanarko[/url] in particular.

Rama was the creator of the design for the "Stellar" Soul cards, a fan favorite as well as admittedly my favorite set of cards. I came to Rama with only a vague idea of a space themed tokusatsu team, and they were able to expand it into an amazing and recognizable line. The first set of Stellars created was Blue, Orange, and Green. Rama had the idea for their mask stars to add a point as they went up the line, as a way to match the mechanics of the cards going into the next one when you play them.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121936/a1e4b1a1511cdbf6abf45abf18f95969a7b2765c.png[/img]

Finally, I wanted to highlight just how much thought Rama put into Stellar Grey's design. The detail of his skeletal armor frame only being vaguely visible in the final card.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121936/70aee4b564474acc67d15f4477ce3441e61deb15.png[/img]

[h2]Wrapping Up...[/h2]

Phew, that's a lot of stuff and those are just some small pieces of the massive amount of iteration that went into making this thing. Let me know if this was something you enjoyed seeing, or what other behind the scenes dev stuff you might like seeing in the future! I didn't even touch on things like music, overworld sprites, duel interface, or area design :V

[h2]In Other News...[/h2]

I released the full Cardaire soundtrack last week, and it's continued to be spread to other streaming platforms this week. If you're one of the two apple music listeners you can catch it over there now!

https://distrokid.com/hyperfollow/aeiou/cardaire-original-videogame-soundtrack

notes.title: v1.1.34 First QOL Update! (Deck Filters)
notes.content:
[h2]Attention Duelists![/h2]

I'm happy to announce the launch of Cardaire's first ever QOL (Quality of Life) update.

I've been excited to get a chance to implement player feedback now that things are stable as far as bugs go. Based on feedback I received over on the [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/3124080/discussions/]Steam Discussion Forum[/url] my first focus has been touching up the Deck Editor interface with a few filters and other adjustments to make it easier to use.

[h2]Full Patch Notes:[/h2]

QOL Updates (woohoo!):
- Updated the deck count display to be a bit easier to read
- Cleaned up the filter buttons with a nicer font and spacing fixes
- Added a "Set" filter to the deck editor for both the bag and deck
- Added a "Card Type" filter to the deck editor for both the bag and deck
- Other various optimizations to make the deck editor run smoother

Bug Fixes:
- Fixed an issue that would cause cards to not resize properly when sent from hand to discard

[h2]In other news...[/h2]

The progenitor of the Stellars Rama Widjanarko posted some absolutely OUT OF THIS WORLD artwork featuring Mulligan and Stellar Knight to celebrate launch. Go check it out!

notes.title: Future Plans and Launch Weekend Bug Roundup
notes.content:
[h1]Howdy pardners![/h1]

It's been a busy launch weekend. Pop was feeling quite generous when buying cards from the player at his card shop, paying as much as thousands of Card Shards for a few common cards. However I've been told Pop's learned his lesson now that his savings have been decimated, and will now pay a reasonable amount per card.

I wanted to take a moment to thank everyone who's been leaving feedback and reporting bugs on the [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/3124080/discussions/]Steam Discussion Forum[/url]. It's helped me immensely to hunt down bugs and get patches shipped fast.

It was also an absolute joy watching players collaborate on card locations, deck strategies, and game knowledge on the forum as well. Genuinely there is nothing I enjoy more then seeing people interact with things I've made, so thank you from the bottom of my teeny tiny little heart.

[h2]Future Plans[/h2]

After a weekend of patching bugs, things are looking stable. I'm working on this game solo, so thank you for your patience while I bash bugs as they pop up. Bugs will always be my top priority, so I may shift back to them as they come up - but I wanted to lay out where my focus will be going forward otherwise.

[h3]QOL Updates[/h3]

I've already seen a few suggestions for QOL updates, so this will be my next major focus. Please continue to bring up things you would like to see, or give input on suggestions of others. It helps me know what to prioritize when I see an idea get more discussion.

I [b]absolutely cannot[/b] promise everything on this list will make it into game but a few popular suggestions on my radar are:
- More filters in the Deck Editor (Card type, set, etc.)
- Selling cards checking your deck as well as your bag
- Improvements to the enemy AI
- Steam Deck support (this may end up needing the trackpad of the Steam Deck to function)

[h3]DLC/Followup Game[/h3]

I think any indie dev could tell you about the pile of ideas that they had to cut before launch. I had to keep the scope of Cardaire as small as possible given my resources as a solo dev, but wanted to give a slice of the world I had envisioned. I'm proud of what I was able to make given my restrictions, but would love the chance to expand on it or make a proper longer sequel. 

The [b]number one thing[/b] that helps towards making a DLC or a full followup game a reality is Cardaire doing well, so I am going to continue to make it the best experience it can be for now.

[h2]Full Patch List[/h2]

I've always hated games who didn't post full patch notes, so I've commited to posting them with updates. These have been included in the minor update Steam announcements, but here is the full list since launch if you we're curious:

- Changed The Masked Duelist behavior so that he no longer soft locks the game if you duel him from behind
- Fixed a bug that was granting XP for selling cards (Sorry Mulligan, I know you were excited to train in swordsmanship but you will have to stick with dueling.)
- Fixed an issue where the VS screen was not removed after a tournament match.
-- If you have an issue with it blocking your hud, it should now clear if you re-enter Junction Hub
- Disabled sell option in store while troubleshooting further
- The collector now correctly hands out set rewards once
- Stellar Knight is now correctly given when opened in a booster pack
- Fixed a npc in Dusty Trail being marked with a duelist bubble
- The Collector should now more consistently be able to read how many special cards you have
- Fixed an issue with the special card hand outs
- Corrected the label for the Dusty Trail slot effect
- Fixed a bug that was causing cards to sell for quite a lot more then intended
- Re-activated the selling feature in Pop's Pop Up Card Swap Shop
- Re enabled selling cards to the shop (For real this time)
-- Selling should now be fixed, but please let me know on the forum if you are getting an unexpected number of cards
- Fixed a graphical error when the masked duelist hands out his card
- Fixed a minor typo on the Relaxed Duelist
- Hid some placeholder overworld sprites that were appearing in Junction Hub
- Further fixes to keep a blue box placeholder sprite from appearing on screen in some situations
- Minor text fixes in Frontier Wilds

[h2]In Other News...[/h2]

Ashmish made some STELLAR art featuring Mulligan and Stellar White. Check it out over on Bluesky or that other website.

notes.title: Steam Next Fest Demo Now Live! (And FAQ)
notes.content:
[h1]Attention Cardaire Duelists![/h1]

The Steam Next Fest Demo is now live! Here are some fast FAQs for ya!

[h2]Where can I leave feedback?[/h2]

The [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/3124080/discussions/]Steam Community Discussion[/url] would be the best place. Unfortunately they don't allow user forum signatures, but we make due.

[h2]How much of the game is in the demo?[/h2]

Only the first set of four (the base set) is available in the demo, and 1/4 of the total game content, give or take.

[h2]Will my progress carry over to the full game when it's released?[/h2]

Almost certainly not, sorry.

[h2]When does the demo end?[/h2]

You'll be able to access "Junction Hub" right after the first boss, this is basically the end point but you are welcome to poke around.

[h2]What platforms can I play the game on?[/h2]

The demo is PC only, but planned launch is for both PC and Mac. I may have to go off Steam for the Mac launch, and it requires a beefier M1 or better Mac, but I don't want to leave out my earpod clad brethren.

[h2]I'm confused, how do I play my cards?[/h2]

You can access the "Tutorial and Practice Interface" from your items in the [Esc] menu to go over the basics again any time. Beyond that you just need to discard for energy during the discard phase, and play the card during your main phase. 

[h2]When is the game launching?[/h2]

By end of year!

[h2]What is the best pack 1 pick 1 in Duskmourn?[/h2]

Valgavoth's Onslaught is beyond absurd, but Dissection Tools is closer behind then most people want to admit.

notes.title: 2024 October Steam Next Fest!
notes.content:
Hello Duelists!

notes.title: Devlog 1: Pixel Pretty Good
notes.content:
*tap tap* Is this thing on?

Oh I'm not speaking into a mic? You're telling me I'm writing a devlog?

Understandable, have a good day sir.

[h2]Where We Are[/h2]

Hey card game fans, I wanted to take a second to check in. How are you? How's the family? Your stomach doing better?

Me? Well I've been busy announcing and tuning-up a videogame! Big shoutout to everyone who has left comments and thrown it a wishlist. Seeing feedback has given me a solid push to get more work done.

Now that the ungodly work of "Making a Steam Store Page" is done, I've shifted focus back to polish. I don't particularly enjoy the marketing aspect of things, but understand it's important to a game's health. It's just hard to spend time making marketing material when my brain says that time could be spent making the game the best it can be. So in general, I've been happy to shift back to working on the game again. The past two weeks my main goal has been touching up some visual elements that were long overdue for a shining.

After [url=https://www.reddit.com/r/PixelArt/comments/1ef5xyb/trying_to_improve_my_path_texture_which_do_you/]consulting the experts over at reddit[/url], I did some work to touch up a lot of the ground and object textures and am loving the result. Check out a preview of that work!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121936/361c4be1e5773560cbc93885b3cb4417c4b500d7.gif[/img]

My other major focus has been touching up the pack opening experience. Everyone knows the real reason to play card games is to inhale the pack fresh air that contains addictive chemicals banned in most countries. So I really want to make the experience of cracking packs as special as possible. Small things like the top ripping off, or a "new" pop-up go a long way. 

Enjoy these extra crunchy compressed gif previews :)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121936/64003f036c7c64bba4f7e7eb09b16aba8d030356.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121936/a6721a5b256f14e26dda16ec5906253bfd97962f.gif[/img]

[h2]Where We're Going[/h2]

Hope you enjoyed this little write-up. The main content for the game is complete at this point, so it's all polish and extra pizzazz from here.

That's all you get for now, bye!
